Same-arm ordered pairs give 2(a−t)_+, different arms give 2[t_+−(t−a)_+−(t−b)_++(t−a−b)_+]; integrating yields a normalized continuous density. At 0, f(0+)=2/L, L² f'(0+)=k(k−3), and integer k≥3 is uniquely determined by a strictly increasing sequence k(k−3). On positive radii the distributional second derivative is L² f''=(4−2k)Σδ_(a_i)+2Σ_{i<j}δ_(a_i+a_j). Since 4−2k<0 and all pair sums involving an unknown positive arm occur strictly to the RIGHT of the least unknown arm, subtracting recovered-arm individual and known-pair atoms iteratively finds both the least remaining length and its multiplicity without generic assumptions; equality/cancellation at larger lengths does not obscure the residual least impulse. Independently verified with exact fractions alongside the rose claim in 220 reconstruction cases including 3≤k≤6 and many equal/additive-colliding values; original full source checker contains further 368 tests and Monte Carlo, inspected but not treated as proof. The arbitrary real lengths follow from deterministic distributional identities and induction.
